STATUS: fail

SUMMARY: One reproduced gap: content appended to the shadow root of a non-target host that stays visible (because it contains a live announcer or top-layer element) is not hidden, while the light-DOM equivalent is. The criteria don't name this root explicitly, so it is a gap against the light-DOM rule rather than a listed criterion. Everything else I probed held, including nested roots, out-of-order revert, row cells, custom roots, host removal, and the flag-off differential against HEAD.

FILES TOUCHED: none (probe files were created and deleted; `git status` matches the start: package.json, ariaHideOutside.ts, ariaHideOutside.test.js, yarn.lock)

FINDINGS:
- [blocking] Mutations inside a non-target shadow root are not observed unless it encloses a target, so an element added to a host that is left visible (it contains an announcer) is not hidden. Repro: `ariaHideOutside([target])` with a sibling host whose shadow root holds `<div data-live-announcer="true">`, then `late = el(sibHost.shadowRoot)` and `await waitFor(() => expect(late).toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden','true'))` → `Received: null`. The light-DOM analog (container holding an announcer, child appended later) passes. Likely fix: observe every shadow root the walker visits that is not hidden, or document the limitation.
- [minor] Pre-existing, not changed by this diff and not probed: calling a revert twice when the call is not on top of the stack splices index -1 and removes another call's observer.

CHECKS:
- Sibling host with inner elements (only host hidden, inner untouched, restored) → pass
- Target that is itself a shadow host (light sibling hidden, host and its content visible) → pass
- Element appended into hidden sibling host's shadow root, two levels deep → pass (no own aria-hidden)
- Light container with children appended later → pass (container hidden, children not)
- Announcer inside non-target sibling host present before call → pass (host not hidden, sibling inside hidden)
- Announcer host: element appended to its shadow root later → FAIL (see blocking finding)
- Element moved from target into shadow root sibling position → pass
- Element moved from hidden sibling host's shadow root into enclosing root → pass (hidden)
- Two calls in different shadow roots, revert first call out of order → pass
- role="row" sibling in shadow root (cells hidden) → pass
- Custom root inside shadow root → pass; custom light root not containing host → pass, no throw
- Revert after host removed from document → pass (no throw, light sibling restored)
- Nested calls in one shadow root, inner revert → pass
- Target inside host within hidden light container → pass
- Re-call after revert on same targets → pass
- keepVisible on a shadow-root element → pass
- Flag-off differential (new vs HEAD copy, same shadow scenario) → pass (identical snapshots)
- Flag-off: shadow sibling and late shadow content not hidden → pass
- `yarn jest packages/@react-aria/overlays` → 201/201 pass

OPEN QUESTIONS: Should content added to a visible non-target shadow host (one holding an announcer or top-layer element) be hidden? If yes, the fix is in the diff; if no, document that the light-DOM rule does not carry over.
